newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Assa Abloy says 9-mo profit jumps 69 pct.
newsitem.headline: Assa Abloy says 9-mo profit jumps 69 pct.

text.p: The world's largest lock maker, Sweden's Assa Abloy AB, on Thursday posted a 69 percent jump in pre-tax profit for the first nine months of 1996, saying it expected a good result for the full year.
Assa Abloy reported pre-tax earnings of 240 million Swedish crowns ($36.4 million) for the nine months to September 30 with sales rising 35 percent to 3.6 billion crowns compared to a year ago.
The company said after adjustments for a negative foreign exchange effect of nine percent, the increase in sales for comparable units was 7.6 percent.
"The growth in Nordic markets has increased during the third quarter," Assa Abloy said in a statement.
"Germany shows stable volumes. Britain has shown a strong growth rate during the third quarter in spite of a continued weak business climate.
"The six percent growth of the group's U.S. units is good and in line with expectations."
Assa Abloy said adverse currency moves had wiped 23 million crowns off results mainly due to the stronger Swedish crown.
However, a negative foreign exchange effect of 12 million crowns on export sales had been eliminated through hedging activities.
Profit per share increased to 2.86 crowns against 1.61 crowns a year ago.
"The expectation of a continued good result development for Assa Abloy in 1996 remains unchanged," the company's chief executive officer Carl-Henric Svanberg said.
-- Belinda Goldsmith, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017 ($ = 6.591 Swedish Crowns)
